findings_qualitative.value: CH+ is detected in absorption in five of six targets and in emission in all, with broad emission over 1000 km/s.

evidence.quote: We detect absorption in five targets, out of the six observed.

claims.hypothesis: Broad CH+ emission arises from shocks driven by hot winds
claims.experiment: Fit emission lines and compare with shock models
claims.result: FWHM 1100-1400 km/s; low velocity C-type shocks reproduce CH+
claims.finding: Emission traces numerous low-velocity shocks in dense gas powered by hot galactic winds

evidence.quote: We find that the CH$^+$ emission lines, which are broader than $1000$  km s$^{-1}$, originate in dense shock waves powered by hot galactic winds.

claims.hypothesis: CH+ absorption traces extended turbulent reservoirs
claims.experiment: Derive radius, mass from absorption linewidth and turbulent energy flux
claims.finding: Large gravitationally bound turbulent reservoirs surround the starburst cores

evidence.quote: extending far outside ($> 10$ kpc) the starburst cores (radii $<1$ kpc)

claims.hypothesis: Outflows alone can sustain the reservoirs
claims.finding: Additional inflows (mergers or cold streams) are required

evidence.quote: However, the mass outflow rates are found to be insufficient to balance the star formation rates.

why_this_method.value: CH+ forms only with supra-thermal energy input and its J=1-0 line is emitted in dense gas yet absorbed in dilute gas

evidence.quote: This line has such a high critical density for excitation that it is emitted only in very dense ($>10^5$  cm$^{-3}$) gas, and is absorbed in low-density gas.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: J-type shocks rejected as far less efficient than C-type for CH+ production

evidence.quote: We conclude that $J$-type shocks are far less efficient than $C$-type shocks to produce CH$^+$.

limitations_admitted.value: Coarse velocity resolution; N(CH+) may be lower limits due to possible saturation
